hazard.summary: Provider 429/retry pressure saturates LiteLLM proxy execution resources, delaying Kubernetes readiness probes and triggering restart-driven availability collapse.
signals: LiteLLM proxy v1.77.7 under sustained provider 429s
Peak load reported at 500 QPS with average load around 60 QPS
all pods failing readiness probes and restarting
separateHealthApp workaround can mask main-process saturation
/health/readiness shares event loop with request processing
Redis call in readiness path competes with proxy traffic

constraints: Control-plane health checks must not depend on the same saturated execution path that provider retries can congest.
Health isolation must still observe main-process liveness; a separate health app must not blindly report healthy when the main proxy is saturated or deadlocked.
Provider retry behavior must be bounded by max attempts and max elapsed time so retry pressure cannot consume the event loop indefinitely.
Readiness failure should remove a pod from routing without creating a restart storm that reduces capacity and amplifies upstream 429 pressure.
Provider 429 handling must emit degraded-state signals visible to orchestration, routing, and operators.
Retry scheduling, cooldown management, logging callbacks, and health probes must have explicit resource and latency budgets.
verification: Run a 60 to 500 QPS load test against LiteLLM with mocked provider 429 responses and measure /health/readiness latency.
Repeat the load test with num_retries: 1 and num_retries: 3 while tracking active tasks, retry queue depth, event-loop lag, and readiness failures.
Simulate Redis latency in the readiness path and verify health responses remain within the configured Kubernetes timeout budget or fail explicitly.
Verify that readiness degradation removes pods from routing without causing synchronized restart storms across all replicas.
If using a separate health app, add a main-process heartbeat/event-loop-lag dependency and prove it reports unhealthy when the main proxy is saturated.
Verify provider 429 pressure emits decision/degradation events that operators can distinguish from generic pod failure.
Confirm bounded retry budgets prevent provider 429s from consuming all execution capacity under sustained load.

constraints: Isolate control-plane health from data-plane retry saturation.
Preserve main-process liveness visibility when health is isolated.
Bound retry pressure with global attempts and elapsed-time budgets.
Prevent readiness failures from creating capacity-reducing restart storms.

impact.operator_impact: Under sustained provider 429s, the proxy may fail readiness checks, restart pods, reduce available capacity, and amplify the load condition it is trying to survive.
impact.business_consequence: Provider throttling can escalate into platform downtime when retry pressure and health orchestration are coupled through shared runtime resources.

notes: Open issue with operator evidence and multi-user corroboration. Original report describes LiteLLM proxy v1.77.7 under sustained provider 429s failing Kubernetes readiness probes and restarting all pods. A later comment argues the separateHealthApp workaround can mask main-process saturation because it may report healthy without observing the main proxy. Treat as a high-signal open receipt, not a confirmed fixed/adopted mitigation. Proposed pattern: control-plane-health-coupled-to-data-plane-backpressure.
